epics.title: E06 — Magic Framework
epics.description:
## Outcome
A data-driven spell architecture where every spell is a content file composed of a delivery (self, projectile, AoE, beam, touch, summon point) and a list of effect operations (damage, world-property stimulus, force, status, summon, transform, displace). Spells never script pairwise interactions: they emit world stimuli (heat, cold, force, light, moisture, charge, life, decay, sound) into the systemic engine (E03), which resolves outcomes through object properties. Casting has a mana resource, cast times, channeling, interruption and botched casts that create new situations.

## Scope
- In: spell schema + validators (src/content), deterministic spell runtime (src/sim), mana, cast lifecycle, delivery types, effect ops, statuses, summons, transformations, displacement, miscasts, light/noise emission, spell hotbar/selection UI, aiming, VFX/SFX cue binding with placeholder visuals, save state, debug tooling, NPC casting. Telemetry emission is left to E34 (Related: spell_cast/spell_miscast/spell_combo events).
- Out: individual spells (mw-e08), learning spells from books (mw-e07), bookshops (mw-e21), final VFX art (mw-e29), final SFX (mw-e28/e38).

## Exit criteria
- A new spell with qualitatively new behaviour can be added as data only (no src/sim change) whenever it uses existing effect ops.
- src/sim/magic and src/content/spells at 100% coverage; replay tests hash-identical for spell-heavy recordings.
- A sorcerer can cast, aim, run out of mana, be interrupted and botch a cast in the greybox testbed.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 Every E06 child bead closed or explicitly deferred.
- EC-2 A fixture spell composed only of existing ops loads and runs with zero code changes (content test).
- EC-3 grep of src/sim/magic contains no spell-id or object-id specific branches (lint rule or test).
- EC-4 Sorcerer core loop (select, aim, cast, interrupt, miscast) demonstrated in the greybox testbed via Playwright e2e.

epics.title: E07 — Spellbook & Magical Learning
epics.description:
## Outcome
Spells are discovered through books, shops, exploration, quests, secrets and experimentation rather than appearing on level-up. Books are inventory items with language, condition, comprehension difficulty and legality; reading and study teach spells; damaged, untranslated and forbidden books create side-goals; experimentation with the world reveals new verbs. Progression unlocks new verbs (Firebolt → Flame Jet → Fire Wall), never +% tiers.

## Scope
- In: book item schema, reading and study, comprehension, damaged/untranslated/forbidden books, experimentation insights, verb-chain progression, grimoire + reader UI, book acquisition hooks, persistence.
- Out: book shops and pricing (mw-e21), spell definitions (mw-e08), generic inventory (mw-e17), world placement of specific books (world-content epics E24–E26).

## Exit criteria
- A sorcerer can find a book, read it, study it and cast the taught spell, all in the greybox testbed.
- At least one spell in the catalogue is reachable only via experimentation, and one only via a verb-chain unlock.
- 100% coverage on learning rules and book schema.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 Every E07 child bead closed or explicitly deferred.
- EC-2 Content validator rejects any progression step whose only difference from its predecessor is numeric.
- EC-3 Playwright e2e: pick up book → read → study → spell appears in grimoire and hotbar → cast succeeds.

epics.title: E08 — Spell Catalogue
epics.description:
## Outcome
An MVP library of ~20 spells across Fire, Frost, Storm, Arcane, Illusion, Alteration, Conjuration, Necromancy, Nature, Light, Shadow, Gravity and Time, emphasising qualitatively different effects: ignition, freezing, force, telekinesis, teleportation, decoys, restraint, summoning, gravity, transformation, light, darkness, water and time. Every spell interacts with the world only through properties and stimuli, and ridiculous combinations are encouraged.

## Scope
- In: spell content files, per-spell automated tests (effects + world interactions), placeholder VFX/SFX cue ids, book item for each spell, school conventions doc, combination test suite.
- Out: engine/runtime (mw-e06), learning (mw-e07), final VFX/SFX assets (asset prompt beads under E28/E29/E37/E38), placement of books in the world (E24–E26).

## Exit criteria
- 19 P1 spells shipped (P2 spells optional for MVP).
- Every spell has unit tests for its effects and integration tests for at least two property-based world interactions.
- Spell combination suite green; "too useful" spells are documented as intentionally allowed.
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 Every E08 P1 child closed.
- EC-2 Content test: every spell file references a school, a book item, a VFX cue and an SFX cue, and has a matching test file.
- EC-3 Combination suite covers every pair of stimulus types emitted by catalogue spells.

epics.title: E21 — Bookshops
epics.description:
## Outcome
Magical bookshops are exciting progression and exploration destinations. A data-authored bookshop definition combines regional stock pools, school specialties, deterministic rotation, rare one-off books, secret back-room stock, stolen and forbidden books, book-specific pricing and a bookseller identity that hooks into dialogue and rumours. Any settlement's bookshop can be authored purely as data.

## Scope
- In: bookshop system rules on top of the generic shop system, stock rules, pricing, legality, bookseller identity hooks, bookshop browsing UI, authoring template + validator, persistence of stock state.
- Out: the Briar Glen bookshop, its NPC, dialogue and book selection (world-content group, E24), generic buy/sell (mw-e20), book items themselves (mw-e07).

## Exit criteria
- A fixture bookshop authored only in data exhibits regional, rotating, rare, secret, stolen and forbidden stock in the greybox testbed.
- 100% coverage on bookshop stock and pricing rules (economy rule per contract §3).
epics.acceptance:
- EC-1 Every E21 child bead closed or explicitly deferred.
- EC-2 The bookshop authoring template validates and a fixture shop passes all bookshop content tests.
- EC-3 Same seed + same in-game date always yields identical stock (determinism test).

items.title: Define zod spell schema with delivery, effect ops and cue ids
items.description:
## Why
Data-driven spells (technical constitution) require a single validated shape so designers add spells as content, not code.

## What
A zod schema in src/content/spells for SpellDefinition: id, school, tier/verb-chain links, cost (mana), castTime, channel, cooldown, delivery {self|touch|projectile|aoe|beam|summonPoint}, effects[] (discriminated union of effect ops), tags, vfxCue, sfxCue, bookId, flags (e.g. tooUseful). Validator produces readable errors with file + JSON path.

## Scope
- In: schema, types, validator, content test harness registration
- In: fixture spells for tests
- Out: runtime execution (e06-spell-pipeline)
- Out: real spells (mw-e08)

## Notes
Effect op union starts with: damage, stimulus, force, status, summon, transform, displace, spawnVolume, light, noise. New ops are code; new spells are data. Unknown ops must fail validation, not be ignored.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given a valid fixture spell file, when validated, then it parses into a typed SpellDefinition with no errors.
- AC-2 [content] Given a spell with an unknown effect op "teleportEverything", when validated, then validation fails naming the file and JSON path effects[0].op.
- AC-3 [content] Given a spell with negative mana cost or castTime, when validated, then validation fails with a range error.
- AC-4 [unit] Given two spell files with the same id, when the catalogue loads, then loading fails with a duplicate-id error listing both files.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a spell whose vfxCue or sfxCue is missing, when validated, then validation fails (placeholders must still be named).

items.title: Run data-driven spells through a cast→deliver→effect pipeline
items.description:
## Why
Magic should feel magical and scale combinatorially; one generic pipeline is what lets 20 spells interact without bespoke code.

## What
As a designer, I want any SpellDefinition to execute through one pipeline so that new spells need only data.
The sim resolves a cast request into: validate (known, resources, cooldown) → cast phase → delivery entity → hit/area resolution → apply effect ops in order to targets and the world. Each op is a registered pure handler; effects are sim events on the event bus that render/audio subscribe to.

## Scope
- In: src/sim/magic pipeline, op registry, delivery entity lifecycle, events (SpellCast, SpellHit, SpellEffectApplied, SpellFizzled)
- In: self and touch delivery (other deliveries in their own beads)
- Out: mana and cast timing (e06-mana-resource, e06-cast-lifecycle)
- Out: projectile/AoE/beam delivery (own beads)
- Out: UI and input (e06-spell-hotbar-ui, e06-casting-input-aiming)

## Notes
No Math.random/Date.now; use injected seeded RNG and clock from e00-sim-core. Op handlers must not branch on spell id or target id — enforce via a lint rule or test that greps src/sim/magic for literal spell ids.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a fixture self-delivery spell with a status op, when cast, then SpellCast then SpellEffectApplied events are emitted in that order within the same tick and the caster has the status.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a fixture spell with three effect ops, when it hits a target, then ops apply in declared order and each emits one SpellEffectApplied event.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a cast request for a spell the caster does not know, when processed, then the cast is rejected with reason "unknown-spell" and no resources are spent.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a recorded input log casting 50 fixture spells, when replayed twice via the replay harness, then final sim state hashes are identical.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a new op handler registered under an existing op name, when registering, then registration throws (no silent override).
- AC-6 [content] Given a spell composed only of existing ops, when added as a new data file, then it casts successfully with zero src/sim changes (fixture test).

items.title: Track mana pool, regeneration and spell costs
items.description:
## Why
A casting resource makes spell choice meaningful and lets running dry create tense moments rather than spam.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want a mana pool that drains when casting and regenerates over time so that I choose spells deliberately.
Mana: current/max, regen per second with a delay after casting, cost reservation for channeled spells, over-cast (casting with insufficient mana) routed to the miscast system rather than a flat refusal when the spell allows it.

## Scope
- In: mana component, regen, spend/refund, HUD-facing events
- In: config data for base values
- Out: HUD bar visuals (mw-e06 hotbar UI shows mana)
- Out: mana potions (items epic, Related: E17 consumables)

## Notes
Stat increases to max mana are allowed but must not be the main progression (anti-grind rule).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given 50/100 mana and a 20-cost spell, when cast completes, then mana is 30 and a ManaChanged event is emitted.
- AC-2 [unit] Given regen 5/s and a 1.5 s post-cast delay, when 3.5 s elapse after a cast, then exactly 10 mana has regenerated.
- AC-3 [unit] Given 10 mana and a 20-cost spell that disallows over-cast, when cast is attempted, then it is rejected with reason "insufficient-mana" and mana is unchanged.
- AC-4 [unit] Given 10 mana and a 20-cost spell that allows over-cast, when cast, then a miscast roll is requested with severity proportional to the 10-mana deficit and mana goes to 0.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a cast interrupted during its cast phase, when interrupted, then 50% of the cost is refunded (configurable).

items.title: Support cast times, channeling, cooldowns and interruption
items.description:
## Why
Cast timing makes sorcerer combat about positioning and reading enemies, and interruption creates risk and stories.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want spells to have wind-up, channel and cooldown timings that enemies can interrupt so that casting is a skill, not a button press.
States: idle → winding (castTime) → released | channeling (tick every N ms, drains mana) → recovery. Interruption sources: poise break from e04 damage model, being grappled/restrained, silence status, caster movement rules per spell (castWhileMoving flag).

## Scope
- In: cast state machine, cooldown tracking, interruption rules, cancel by player
- Out: animation (render/game layer)
- Out: botched cast outcomes (e06-botched-casts)

## Notes
Interruption during the final 20% of wind-up should be eligible for a miscast instead of a clean fizzle (hook for e06-botched-casts).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a spell with castTime 800 ms, when cast begins, then no delivery is spawned before 800 ms of sim time and exactly one at 800 ms.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a channeled spell ticking every 250 ms at 4 mana/tick, when channeled for 1 s, then 4 ticks apply and 16 mana is drained.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a caster winding up, when it receives a hit that breaks poise, then the cast enters interrupted state, emits SpellInterrupted and spawns no delivery.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a spell with cooldown 5 s, when recast after 4.9 s, then it is rejected with reason "cooldown" and after 5.0 s it succeeds.
- AC-5 [unit] Given castWhileMoving=false, when the caster moves more than 0.5 m during wind-up, then the cast is cancelled without miscast and with refund.
- AC-6 [unit] Given interruption in the last 20% of wind-up, when interrupted, then a miscast request is emitted instead of a clean fizzle.

items.title: Emit world-property stimuli from spell effects into the world sim
items.description:
## Why
The constitution's top architectural rule: spells interact with the world via properties, never "Fireball + Rope" scripts.

## What
As a designer, I want spell effects to emit typed stimuli (heat, cold, force, light, moisture, charge, life, decay, sound) with magnitude, radius and duration so that the E03 engine decides what burns, freezes, conducts, grows or rots.
The stimulus op writes into the E03 element-propagation / property system at a point, along a ray, or in a volume. Persistent spell volumes (fire wall, ice sheet, rain) register as ongoing stimulus sources.

## Scope
- In: stimulus op handler, stimulus vocabulary mapping to E03 property rules, persistent spell-sourced stimulus volumes
- In: test fixtures with generic property-tagged objects (flammable crate, wet floor, conductive chain, fragile vase)
- Out: the propagation rules themselves (e03-element-propagation)
- Out: light field integration (e06-spell-light-noise-emission)

## Notes
Tests must use property-tagged generic fixtures, never named props. If a desired behaviour needs a new stimulus type, add it to the vocabulary here and the rule in E03 — Related: coordinate with Core group for any new property.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given any object tagged flammable inside a heat stimulus ≥ its ignition threshold, when 1 sim second passes, then it is burning.
- AC-2 [integration] Given any wet or water-surface tile inside a cold stimulus ≥ freeze threshold, when applied, then it gains the frozen property for the stimulus duration plus melt time.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a charge stimulus hitting a conductive object that touches other conductive or wet objects, when applied, then charge propagates to connected objects per E03 rules.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a stimulus op with radius 0 and no ray, when validated, then content validation fails ("stimulus needs point radius, ray or volume").
- AC-5 [integration] Given a heat stimulus and a cold stimulus overlapping a burning object in the same tick, when resolved, then the result is deterministic and identical across two replays.
- AC-6 [unit] Given src/sim/magic, when scanned by the property-only lint test, then no code references object ids or spell ids in interaction logic.

items.title: Deliver spells as physical projectiles with collision and arcs
items.description:
## Why
Projectiles are the most common spell delivery and must feel precise and physical for sorcerer combat.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want projectile spells with speed, gravity, lifetime, pierce and bounce parameters so that bolts, lobbed orbs and ricochets all come from data.
Projectile collides with hurtboxes (damage model) and world geometry; on impact it applies on-hit ops and optional impact AoE; it carries its stimulus along its path (e.g. heat trail) if configured.

## Scope
- In: projectile delivery entity, sweep collision (no tunnelling), impact ops, pierce/bounce counts, lifetime expiry ops
- Out: homing (post-MVP, Related: future spell)
- Out: arrows (e05-bow-core)

## Notes
Share collision sweep utilities with e05-bow-core if available; do not depend on it.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a projectile at 60 m/s and a 0.1 m wall, when simulated at the fixed timestep, then it impacts the wall (no tunnelling) in 100% of 1000 randomized seeded trials.
- AC-2 [unit] Given gravity 9.8 and launch angle 30°, when simulated, then the impact point is within 5 cm of the analytic ballistic solution.
- AC-3 [unit] Given bounce=2, when the projectile hits walls three times, then it bounces twice and applies impact ops on the third.
- AC-4 [unit] Given lifetime 3 s and no impact, when 3 s pass, then onExpire ops apply at its position and the entity is removed.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a projectile with a heat trail stimulus passing over a flammable object, when it passes within 0.5 m, then the object receives heat per E03 rules.

items.title: Deliver spells as AoE volumes, cones and reflecting beams
items.description:
## Why
Battlefield manipulation needs areas, cones and beams, and beams that reflect enable light puzzles (puzzle constitution).

## What
As a sorcerer, I want sphere, cone, line/wall and ground-decal volumes plus continuous beams so that shockwaves, fire walls and light rays are all data.
Volumes: instant or persistent with tick rate, falloff curve, line-of-sight check option. Beams: raycast each tick, length, width, reflect off objects tagged reflective up to N bounces, blocked by opaque solids.

## Scope
- In: volume shapes, persistence, tick, falloff, LOS option; beam raycast, reflection, max bounces
- Out: stimulus semantics (e06-world-stimulus-emitters)
- Out: specific spells (mw-e08)

## Notes
Beam reflection uses the reflective property only — any mirror, polished shield or ice surface tagged reflective works.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a 4 m sphere with linear falloff, when targets stand at 0, 2 and 4.1 m, then they receive 100%, 50% and 0% magnitude.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a 60° cone of range 6 m, when a target is at 35° off-axis, then it is not affected; at 25°, it is.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a persistent volume with tick 500 ms and duration 3 s, when it expires, then exactly 6 ticks were applied.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a beam hitting an object tagged reflective, when maxBounces=2, then the beam reflects by the surface normal and stops after the second reflection.
- AC-5 [unit] Given an AoE with requiresLOS, when a target is fully behind an opaque wall, then it receives no effect.
- AC-6 [perf] Given 8 persistent volumes and 4 beams active in the stress scene, when simulated, then magic sim cost p95 ≤ 1.0 ms per tick on the reference machine.

items.title: Apply spell forces: impulse, knockback, pull and lift
items.description:
## Why
"Throw enemies through furniture" is a core magic fantasy; forces must work identically on creatures and loose objects.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want force ops (radial push, directional impulse, point pull, sustained lift) so that I can hurl, drag and float things.
Force respects weight: magnitude / mass → displacement; creatures convert excess force into stagger/knockdown via the damage model; objects colliding at speed apply impact damage and break fragile things.

## Scope
- In: force op handler for rigid bodies and creatures, mass scaling, knockdown thresholds, impact damage on collision
- Out: telekinetic grab/hold (Mage Hand spell uses a sustained-lift + tether op defined here but tuned in mw-e08)

## Notes
Heavy objects (weight property above threshold) should visibly resist rather than ignore force.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a 10 kg and a 40 kg object at equal distance from a radial push of 200 N·s, when applied, then the lighter object's velocity is 4× the heavier's.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a creature pushed into any object tagged fragile at ≥ 6 m/s, when they collide, then the object breaks and the creature takes collision damage.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a creature with poise 50 hit by force equivalent to 70 poise damage, when applied, then it is knocked down.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an object tagged anchored or weight above the max-liftable threshold, when a lift op is applied, then it does not leave the ground and a ForceResisted event is emitted.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a point pull, when targets reach the pull centre, then they stop within 0.5 m instead of oscillating (damped).

items.title: Apply buffs, debuffs and statuses with stacking and dispel
items.description:
## Why
Restrain, levitate, slow, silence and ward effects are how many spells change situations without damage.

## What
As a designer, I want a data-driven status system (duration, stack rule, tick ops, modifiers, tags, break conditions) so that spells like Grasping Vines or Levitate are composed rather than coded.
Statuses: rooted, slowed, levitating, silenced, frozen-solid, burning (mirrors world state), warded, revealed, invisible-to-senses (hook for AI).

## Scope
- In: status definitions in content, apply/refresh/stack/expire, break conditions (e.g. rooted breaks when the root object burns), dispel by tag
- Out: transformations (e06-transformation-framework)
- Out: AI reaction to statuses (E11/E12)

## Notes
Break conditions must be property-driven: "rooted breaks if the restraining entity loses the intact property" rather than "vines break on fire".
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a status with stack rule "refresh", when applied twice 2 s apart with 5 s duration, then it expires 7 s after first application.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a status with stack rule "stack(max 3)", when applied 4 times, then stack count is 3.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a rooted status whose source entity is destroyed, when the source is removed, then the status ends in the same tick.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a dispel of tag "magical", when applied to a target with 2 magical and 1 mundane status, then only the 2 magical statuses are removed.
- AC-5 [content] Given a status definition referencing an unknown modifier stat, when validated, then validation fails.
- AC-6 [integration] Given a silenced caster, when it attempts a cast, then the cast is rejected with reason "silenced".

items.title: Summon temporary creatures and objects with allegiance and caps
items.description:
## Why
Summoning (Animate Bones, Mirror Self decoys, conjured objects) is a qualitatively different verb from damage.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want summon ops that spawn a creature or object archetype for a duration, optionally consuming nearby world material, so that summons feel grounded in the world.
Parameters: archetype id (from creature schema), duration, allegiance (caster/neutral), maxActive per caster, requiresMaterial {property tag, radius, count} (e.g. remains), on-expire ops, command hooks (follow/stay/attack).

## Scope
- In: summon op, material consumption by property tag, lifetime, cap enforcement (oldest dismissed), allegiance faction assignment
- Out: summon AI behaviours (E11/E12 — Related: follow/guard behaviours)
- Out: specific summons (mw-e08)

## Notes
Material requirement uses property tags such as remains, not specific corpse ids.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given maxActive=2 and two active summons, when a third is summoned, then the oldest is dismissed with its on-expire ops and the new one spawns.
- AC-2 [unit] Given requiresMaterial {tag: remains, radius: 6, count: 1} and no remains within 6 m, when cast, then the cast fails with reason "no-material", emits a SpellFizzled event and refunds 100% mana.
- AC-3 [unit] Given remains within range, when the summon succeeds, then the consumed remains entity is removed and the summon spawns at its position.
- AC-4 [unit] Given duration 30 s, when 30 s pass, then the summon is removed and on-expire ops apply at its location.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a summon with allegiance caster, when hostile creatures perceive it, then they treat it as hostile per faction rules.

items.title: Temporarily transform creatures into other archetypes and back
items.description:
## Why
Polymorph-style effects are iconic "wait, I can do that?" magic and must restore state safely.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want a transform op that swaps a creature's archetype (body, senses, attacks, properties) for a duration and restores it exactly so that turning a guard into a chicken is safe and systemic.
Preserves identity, health ratio, inventory, quest/dialogue state, alert memory; the new form uses its own senses/locomotion/properties (a transformed creature that is now flammable burns).

## Scope
- In: transform op, snapshot/restore, health ratio mapping, size-safe restore (find free space), resist rules via creature tags
- Out: player self-transformation (post-MVP, Related: future spell)
- Out: specific forms (mw-e08 Polymorph)

## Notes
Restore must handle the form being killed (original dies? or reverts with 1 HP — configurable per spell) and not enough space to restore (push to nearest free space).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a creature at 60% health transformed into a form with different max HP, when transformed and restored, then health ratio is 60% in both forms (minus damage taken).
- AC-2 [unit] Given a transformed creature, when the duration ends, then inventory, faction, dialogue flags and identity id are byte-identical to the pre-transform snapshot.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a creature tagged immune-transform, when targeted, then the op fails with reason "resisted" and emits SpellResisted.
- AC-4 [unit] Given the transformed form is killed and the spell sets onFormDeath=revert, when killed, then the original reverts with 1 HP and a stagger status.
- AC-5 [unit] Given insufficient space to restore a large creature, when reverting, then it is placed at the nearest free position within 3 m, or the revert is deferred until space exists.
- AC-6 [integration] Given a save made while a creature is transformed, when loaded, then the transform remaining duration and snapshot restore correctly.

items.title: Teleport and swap positions with collision-safe placement
items.description:
## Why
Teleportation opens traversal routes (classes change possibilities) and must never put the player inside walls.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want displace ops (teleport-to-point, swap-with-target, short dash) with safe placement so that Blink-like spells are reliable and exploitable.
Validates destination: capsule fits, not inside solid geometry, optional line-of-sight requirement, ledge/floor snapping, falls through if no floor (story!).

## Scope
- In: displace op handler, capsule fit test, LOS option, nearest-valid fallback search, swap semantics
- Out: specific spells (mw-e08 Blink)

## Notes
Teleporting over a chasm with no floor intentionally drops the caster — failure creates stories.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a teleport target inside a wall, when resolved, then the caster lands at the nearest valid point along the aim ray before the wall, never inside geometry (1000 seeded fuzz trials).
- AC-2 [unit] Given requiresLOS and a target point behind a closed door, when cast, then it fails with reason "no-line-of-sight".
- AC-3 [unit] Given a swap-with-target op on a creature too large to fit at the caster's position, when cast, then the swap is rejected with reason "no-space" and mana is refunded.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a teleport destination with no floor within 1 m, when cast, then the caster arrives at the destination and begins falling.

items.title: Resolve botched casts into data-driven miscast outcomes
items.description:
## Why
Failure creates stories: a botched spell should produce a new situation (smoke, a wild blink, a sudden frost) instead of a dull "fizzle".

## What
As a sorcerer, I want interrupted, over-cast or poorly-understood spells to sometimes misfire in school-flavoured ways so that mistakes are memorable.
Miscast triggers: over-cast (mana deficit), late interruption, low comprehension (from E07), casting while a status like drenched/charged conflicts. A weighted miscast table per school (and optional per spell) picks outcomes composed from existing ops: backfire on self at reduced magnitude, random-direction delivery, harmless cosmetic, loud noise event, stimulus burst at caster (e.g. frost puddle, smoke).

## Scope
- In: miscast request handling, severity calculation, weighted tables in content, seeded selection, MiscastOccurred event
- Out: comprehension model (e07-comprehension-study)
- Out: VFX for miscasts (placeholder cue per school)

## Notes
Miscast outcomes must never softlock or instakill: cap self-damage at 25% max HP. Every outcome reuses existing ops so miscasts interact with the world too (a fire miscast can ignite the bookshelf you are standing next to).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a miscast request with severity 0.1, when resolved with a fixed seed, then the outcome is drawn from the table's low-severity band and is deterministic across runs.
- AC-2 [unit] Given any miscast outcome, when applied to a caster at full HP, then self-damage never exceeds 25% max HP (property test over all tables).
- AC-3 [integration] Given a Fire-school miscast producing a heat burst at the caster, when a flammable object is within the burst radius, then it ignites via E03 rules.
- AC-4 [content] Given a miscast table whose weights sum to 0 or referencing an unknown op, when validated, then validation fails.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a miscast outcome "loud", when applied, then a noise event of the configured loudness is emitted for stealth/AI.
- AC-6 [manual] Given a playtest of 20 deliberate over-casts, when observed, then at least 3 distinct outcome types occur and testers describe them as funny or interesting rather than punishing.

items.title: Make spells emit light and noise that stealth and AI perceive
items.description:
## Why
Magic must feed the same world systems as the thief: a glowing spell reveals you, a Thunderclap wakes the dungeon.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want spells to contribute light to the light field and noise events to sound propagation so that casting has stealth consequences and light spells solve darkness.
Light op: intensity, radius, colour tag, duration, attach-to (caster/projectile/point). Noise: per-phase loudness (wind-up, release, impact).

## Scope
- In: light op writing to e03-light-field, spell noise events into e09-sound-propagation, per-phase loudness data
- Out: visual lighting (render)
- Out: AI reaction logic (E11)

## Notes
Light spells should also be usable by creatures (light-averse creatures flee via their own property rules in E12).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a dark room with light level 0.05, when a light op of intensity 0.8 radius 6 m is placed at its centre, then the light field query at 3 m returns ≥ 0.4.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a projectile carrying a light op, when it moves, then the light field updates at its position each tick and clears at its previous position within 1 tick.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a spell with impact loudness 90, when it impacts, then a noise event with loudness 90 is emitted at the impact position.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a light op with duration 10 s, when 10 s pass, then its light field contribution is removed.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a spell with no noise data, when validated, then it defaults to school default loudness rather than silence.

items.title: Aim and cast spells with reticle, ground targeting and cancel
items.description:
## Why
Sorcerer combat must feel precise and responsive with keyboard and mouse first.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want to aim projectiles with a reticle, place AoEs with a ground marker, hold to channel and cancel with a key so that casting feels deliberate.
Game layer binds input actions → sim cast requests; targeting modes per delivery (reticle, ground, self, target-lock); invalid target feedback (red marker) before committing.

## Scope
- In: game-layer casting controller, targeting modes, placeholder ground marker, input bindings through the action map, gamepad fallback
- Out: hotbar/selection (e06-spell-hotbar-ui)
- Out: final reticle art (asset beads)

## Notes
Latency budget: input-to-cast-start ≤ 100 ms (one render frame + sim tick).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a projectile spell selected, when the cast action is pressed, then a cast request with the camera-reticle aim ray is sent to the sim within the same frame.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a ground-targeted AoE and an aim point beyond max range, when previewed, then the marker clamps to max range and is flagged invalid if no floor exists.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a channeled spell, when the cast action is released, then channeling stops within one sim tick.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed, when a scripted player selects, aims and casts a fixture projectile at a dummy, then the dummy registers a hit.
- AC-5 [perf] Given the reference machine, when measuring input-to-cast-start, then p95 ≤ 100 ms.

items.title: Select spells from a hotbar and quick-select wheel with mana HUD
items.description:
## Why
Combining spells needs fast switching; a sorcerer with 15 spells cannot rely on a menu.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want 8 hotbar slots plus a hold-to-open quick-select wheel and a visible mana bar so that I can switch spells mid-fight.
Shows icon (placeholder), cost, cooldown sweep, unaffordable state, channel indicator; drag from grimoire to slot; slot state persists in saves.

## Scope
- In: hotbar UI, quick-select wheel (slows sim time to 25% while open, configurable), mana bar, keybinds 1–8, gamepad wheel
- Out: grimoire (e07-grimoire-ui)
- Out: final icon art (asset prompt beads per spell)

## Notes
Time-slow while wheel is open is an accessibility option (E31); default on.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given spells in slots 1–3, when key 2 is pressed, then the selected spell becomes slot 2 and a SpellSelected event fires.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a spell on cooldown, when rendered, then the slot shows remaining cooldown in 0.1 s resolution and is marked unavailable.
- AC-3 [integration] Given mana below a slot's cost and over-cast disallowed, when rendered, then the slot shows the unaffordable state.
- AC-4 [integration] Given an empty slot, when its key is pressed, then nothing is selected and no error is thrown.
- AC-5 [integration] Given hotbar assignments, when saved and reloaded, then all 8 slot assignments are restored.
- AC-6 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed, when the quick-select wheel is held, then sim time scale is 0.25 until release.

items.title: Bind spell events to placeholder VFX and SFX cues
items.description:
## Why
Magic must look and sound magical even in grey-box; placeholders unblock gameplay until the art pass (gameplay is never blocked by final art).

## What
As a developer, I want spell events (wind-up, release, travel, impact, persistent, miscast) to trigger named VFX and SFX cues so that swapping placeholders for final assets is a data change.
Cue registry maps cue id → placeholder effect (coloured particles per school, primitive meshes) and placeholder sound; missing cue logs a warning and plays a school default.

## Scope
- In: cue registry, event→cue binding in src/game, school-coloured placeholder particle presets, placeholder SFX hooks
- Out: final VFX (E29 asset beads)
- Out: final SFX (E28/E38 asset beads)

## Notes
Cue naming follows asset ID convention: vfx-spell-<spell>-<phase>, sfx-spell-<spell>-<phase>.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a spell impact event with vfxCue "vfx-spell-ember-impact", when emitted, then the VFX system receives a spawn request for that cue at the impact position.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a cue id with no registered asset, when triggered, then the school default placeholder plays and one warning is logged per cue id (not per trigger).
- AC-3 [content] Given every spell in the catalogue, when validated, then each referenced cue id matches the naming convention.
- AC-4 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed, when every catalogue spell is cast in sequence, then no console errors occur and a screenshot sanity check detects non-background pixels at each impact.

items.title: Persist mana, cooldowns and active spell effects in saves
items.description:
## Why
Save-game stability is a technical pillar; a fire wall or summon must survive save/load exactly.

## What
Serialize mana, cooldowns, in-progress channel state (cancelled on load), persistent volumes, summons and statuses into the versioned save format with round-trip and migration tests.

## Scope
- In: magic save section, round-trip tests, migration test scaffold
- Out: known spells and study progress (e07-learning-save-state)
- Out: transform snapshots (e06-transformation-framework)

## Notes
In-flight projectiles are dropped on save (documented) unless trivial to keep.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a sim with 2 persistent volumes, 1 summon and 3 statuses, when saved and loaded, then state hashes of the magic subsystem match.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a save while channeling, when loaded, then the channel is cancelled and no mana is lost beyond ticks already applied.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a save from magic schema v1, when loaded by v2 code, then the migration test passes.

items.title: Let creatures and NPCs cast catalogue spells through the same pipeline
items.description:
## Why
Enemy mages should obey the same rules as the player so that interrupts, miscasts and world interactions apply to them too.

## What
As a designer, I want creature definitions to list spells with usage hints so that goblin shamans and liches cast via the standard pipeline.
Exposes a cast-request API for AI; creature mana optional; AI can be interrupted and miscast.

## Scope
- In: creature schema extension for spells (via E12 hooks), AI cast API, tests
- Out: AI decision-making about when to cast (E11 — Related: combat behaviours)

## Notes
Player-learnable spells dropped as books by enemy casters is handled in e07-book-acquisition-hooks.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a creature with a fixture projectile spell, when AI requests a cast at a target, then the pipeline processes it identically to a player cast (same events).
- AC-2 [unit] Given a creature caster hit hard during wind-up, when poise breaks, then its cast is interrupted.
- AC-3 [content] Given a creature referencing an unknown spell id, when validated, then validation fails.

items.title: Add magic debug commands and stimulus visualisation
items.description:
## Why
Fast content creation needs designers to grant spells, ignore mana and see stimuli while testing combinations.

## What
Debug console commands: spell.grant <id|all>, spell.infiniteMana, spell.noCooldown, spell.forceMiscast <table>, spell.reload (hot-reload spell JSON); overlay drawing active stimulus volumes, beams and summon lifetimes.

## Scope
- In: console commands, hot reload of spell content in dev builds, debug overlay
- Out: general console (e33-debug-console)

## Notes
Hot reload re-validates; invalid file keeps the previous version and prints errors.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given the debug console, when "spell.grant all" runs, then every catalogue spell is known and assignable.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a spell file edited with an invalid value, when hot-reloaded, then the previous definition remains active and the validation error is printed.
- AC-3 [integration] Given spell.infiniteMana on, when casting 100 spells, then mana never decreases.

items.title: Define book item schema: spell, language, condition, legality
items.description:
## Why
Magic is learned primarily from books (constitution §4); books need a rich, validated data shape.

## What
Zod schema for BookItem extending the inventory item: bookId, title, author, school, teaches (spellId | insight | lore-only), pages (text blocks), language, comprehensionDifficulty (0–1), studyMinutes (in-game), condition {intact|damaged(missingPages[])}, legality {legal|forbidden}, rarity, coverArtId, flags (unique, cursed-whispers).

## Scope
- In: schema + validator + fixtures
- In: registration with inventory item types
- Out: learning runtime (e07-spellbook-learning)
- Out: shop stock (mw-e21)

## Notes
Cover art id follows asset convention: ui-book-cover-<bookId>.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given a valid fixture book teaching a known spell, when validated, then it parses and registers as an inventory item of type book.
- AC-2 [content] Given a book whose teaches references an unknown spell id, when validated, then validation fails naming the book and spell id.
- AC-3 [content] Given a damaged book whose missingPages index exceeds its page count, when validated, then validation fails.
- AC-4 [unit] Given two book definitions teaching the same spell, when loaded, then both are allowed (multiple sources per spell).

items.title: Learn spells by reading and studying book items
items.description:
## Why
Spells should come from discovery, not level-ups; reading a newly bought grimoire should be a moment.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want to read a book and study it for some in-game time so that I learn its spell and can cast it.
Read action opens the book (lore always readable); Study action advances in-game time (resting/at a desk bonus), accumulates study progress; at 100% the spell enters the known-spells registry and a SpellLearned event fires. Non-sorcerer classes can read lore but only learn if the spell allows (e.g. Light scrolls).

## Scope
- In: known-spells registry, study progress per book, study time consumption, class gating, events
- Out: comprehension/partial understanding (e07-comprehension-study)
- Out: reader UI (e07-book-reader-ui)

## Notes
Study can be interrupted (e.g. an ambush) and resumes from saved progress.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a book with studyMinutes 60 and no bonuses, when the player studies for 60 in-game minutes, then the spell is known and SpellLearned {spellId, source: bookId} fires once.
- AC-2 [unit] Given study at a desk-tagged object with a 1.5× bonus, when studying 40 minutes, then progress is 100%.
- AC-3 [unit] Given study interrupted at 30 minutes by a hostile entering Alerted state nearby, when interrupted, then progress is 50% and resuming later completes after 30 more minutes.
- AC-4 [unit] Given an already-known spell, when its book is studied, then no duplicate learn occurs and the book is flagged "known" instead.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a knight reading a sorcerer-only book, when attempting to study, then it is rejected with reason "class" while lore pages remain readable.
- AC-6 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed, when the player picks up a fixture book, studies it and casts its spell, then the cast succeeds.

items.title: Model comprehension so hard books teach unstable spells first
items.description:
## Why
Difficult books should be a challenge, not a lock; casting a half-understood spell is a botched-cast story generator.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want difficult books to be learnable early at low comprehension so that I can cast advanced spells unreliably until I understand them.
Comprehension = f(book difficulty, related known spells in same school, insights, reference books owned). Below threshold 1.0 the spell is "unstable": miscast chance scales with (1 − comprehension). Re-study or related learning raises comprehension.

## Scope
- In: comprehension formula in data, unstable spell state, miscast chance hook into e06-botched-casts, UI-facing values
- Out: miscast outcomes (e06-botched-casts)

## Notes
Anti-grind: comprehension rises from knowledge (books, insights, related spells), not from casting count alone.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given difficulty 0.8 and no related knowledge, when learned, then comprehension is 0.2 and the spell is flagged unstable.
- AC-2 [unit] Given comprehension 0.2, when cast 1000 times with a seeded RNG, then miscast rate is 80% ± 3%.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the player learns two more spells of the same school, when comprehension is recomputed, then it increases by the configured per-related-spell bonus and caps at 1.0.
- AC-4 [unit] Given comprehension reaches 1.0, when computed, then the unstable flag clears and no comprehension miscasts occur.
- AC-5 [content] Given a comprehension config with negative bonuses, when validated, then validation fails.

items.title: Restore damaged books by finding their missing pages
items.description:
## Why
Damaged books turn a spell into an exploration hook: the rest of the pages are somewhere in the monastery.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want a damaged book to teach a partial version of its spell and point me towards missing pages so that finding pages completes it.
Missing pages are separate page items (loot) linked by bookId; a damaged book teaches nothing, lore-only, or an unstable variant as configured; combining pages restores the book.

## Scope
- In: page items, combine action, partial-teach behaviour, restoration event
- Out: placement of pages in the world (E24–E26 content)

## Notes
Missing page text may hint at location (Related: world-content group authors hints).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a damaged book missing pages 3 and 7 configured partialTeach=unstable, when studied, then the spell is learned with comprehension capped at 0.5.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the player holds both missing page items, when combining, then the book becomes intact, the page items are consumed and the comprehension cap lifts.
- AC-3 [unit] Given the player holds only page 3, when combining, then the book remains damaged with only page 7 missing.
- AC-4 [content] Given a page item referencing a book that is not damaged, when validated, then validation fails.

items.title: Translate books written in unknown languages
items.description:
## Why
Untranslated books create quests and reasons to talk to scholars and find lexicons — curiosity rewarded.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want books in unknown languages to be unreadable until I obtain a lexicon or a translation so that decoding knowledge feels earned.
Languages are data; the player knows languages via lexicon items or NPC translation service (dialogue action); partially known languages show garbled text proportional to knowledge.

## Scope
- In: language registry, known-language state, lexicon items, translate action hook for dialogue, garbled text renderer data
- Out: NPC translator dialogue content (E22/E24)

## Notes
Garbling is deterministic per book + knowledge level so the same text appears on re-read.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a book in "Old Tessic" and no knowledge, when read, then study is disabled with reason "language" and pages render garbled.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the player acquires the Old Tessic lexicon item, when reading, then the book is studyable.
- AC-3 [unit] Given 50% language knowledge, when rendering page text, then the same deterministic ~50% of words are garbled on every read.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a dialogue action "translate book X", when executed, then the book gains a translated flag and is studyable regardless of language knowledge.

items.title: Give forbidden books social risk and whispering side effects
items.description:
## Why
Forbidden knowledge is tempting; carrying or reading it should create risk and stories rather than a simple lock.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want forbidden books to teach powerful spells at a social cost so that I decide whether to be seen with them.
Forbidden books are contraband: guards/NPCs who perceive the player reading or openly casting forbidden-school spells react (disposition drop, confiscation attempt, alert). Some carry "whispers" side effects (noise events at night, attracting certain creatures).

## Scope
- In: legality flag handling, witness detection via perception hooks, disposition/world-state consequences, whisper effect
- Out: guard dialogue content (E22/E24)
- Out: buying/selling forbidden stock (e21-stolen-forbidden-stock)

## Notes
Necromancy school spells (e.g. Animate Bones) come from forbidden books in the MVP.

**Integration note:** Promoted — Animate Bones (P1/m2) is taught by a forbidden book.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given an NPC with a lawful disposition that perceives the player reading a forbidden book, when perception succeeds, then a ContrabandWitnessed event fires and the NPC's disposition drops by the configured amount.
- AC-2 [integration] Given no witness has line of sight, when the player reads a forbidden book, then no consequence fires.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a book with whispers, when carried in inventory between 22:00 and 04:00 in-game, then a quiet noise event is emitted every 60 s at the player position.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a book dropped or stashed, when whispers would emit, then they emit at the book's location instead.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a forbidden spell learned, when cast unseen, then no ContrabandWitnessed event fires.

items.title: Discover spell insights and variants through world experimentation
items.description:
## Why
"Wait… I can do that?" — some magic should be discovered by experimenting, not bought.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want casting my spells in unusual world situations to occasionally reveal an insight so that experimentation teaches new verbs.
Insight rules are data: trigger = (spell-sourced stimulus type, target property/state, optional second stimulus) observed by the sim; reward = new spell, spell variant, or comprehension boost. Example rules (property-based): cold stimulus on a water surface → insight "ice bridge" (unlocks Frostglass surface variant); force stimulus on a burning object → insight "flung flame".

## Scope
- In: insight rule schema, observer on stimulus-resolution events, one-time unlocks, InsightDiscovered event + journal entry
- Out: the unlocked spells themselves (mw-e08)

## Notes
Rules may only reference stimulus types and property tags, never object or spell ids for triggers (validator enforces).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given an insight rule {stimulus: cold, targetProperty: water-surface}, when a player-sourced cold stimulus freezes any water surface, then InsightDiscovered fires once and the reward is granted.
- AC-2 [unit] Given the same condition caused by a non-player source (a frost trap), when resolved, then no insight fires.
- AC-3 [unit] Given an insight already discovered, when its trigger recurs, then nothing is granted again.
- AC-4 [content] Given an insight rule whose trigger references an object id, when validated, then validation fails ("triggers must use properties").
- AC-5 [integration] Given a save after discovering an insight, when loaded, then the insight remains discovered.

items.title: Unlock follow-on spell verbs through mastery and advanced books
items.description:
## Why
The anti-grind rule: progression unlocks new verbs (Firebolt → Flame Jet → Fire Wall), not +12% tiers.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want mastering a spell to open its next verb, learnable by study, insight or advanced book, so that growth changes what I can do.
Verb chain data: spell.next[] with unlock requirements (comprehension 1.0, N meaningful uses — e.g. hits on distinct target types, an insight, or owning an advanced book). A content validator rejects chain steps that differ only numerically from their predecessor (same delivery + same op types).

## Scope
- In: verb chain data, unlock evaluation, integration with e19 progression model, anti-grind validator
- Out: specific chains (mw-e08: Ember/Firebolt/Flame Jet/Fire Wall, Mage Hand → Telekinetic Throw & Catch)

## Notes
"Meaningful uses" counts distinct contexts (distinct property tags affected), not raw cast count.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given Firebolt with next Flame Jet requiring comprehension 1.0 and 5 distinct affected property tags, when both are met, then Flame Jet becomes studyable and a VerbUnlocked event fires.
- AC-2 [unit] Given 50 casts affecting only 1 property tag, when evaluated, then Flame Jet remains locked.
- AC-3 [content] Given a chain step with the same delivery and op types as its predecessor differing only in magnitudes, when validated, then validation fails with "numeric-only progression".
- AC-4 [unit] Given an advanced book that teaches a chain step directly, when studied before requirements are met, then the spell is learned but unstable (comprehension ≤ 0.5).
- AC-5 [integration] Given the e19 progression model, when a verb unlocks, then it is recorded as a capability unlock.

items.title: Read books in a page-turning reader with a study action
items.description:
## Why
Books are the sorcerer's core reward; reading one should feel like opening a treasure, not a tooltip.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want to open a book into a two-page reader showing lore, diagrams and a Study button with time estimate so that reading is a moment.
Shows garbled text for unknown language, torn-page placeholders for missing pages, forbidden warning, comprehension estimate, "already known" state.

## Scope
- In: reader UI, study action with time estimate, placeholder parchment/page art, keyboard + gamepad navigation, text scaling via settings
- Out: final book/parchment art (asset prompt beads)

## Notes
Honour E31 text sizing and dyslexia-friendly font option if available.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a book with 6 pages, when opened, then pages 1–2 show and next/prev keys navigate in pairs without going past the last page.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a damaged book, when a missing page is shown, then a torn-page placeholder renders with the text "Pages missing".
- AC-3 [integration] Given the Study button, when pressed, then the displayed estimate matches the sim's computed remaining study minutes.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the player is in combat (Alerted/Combat nearby), when Study is pressed, then it is disabled with a tooltip reason.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed, when a fixture book is opened and closed with the keyboard, then no console errors occur.

items.title: Browse known spells, insights and verb chains in the grimoire
items.description:
## Why
The grimoire is the sorcerer's trophy case and planning tool — seeing locked next verbs motivates exploration.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want a grimoire listing known spells by school with description, cost, comprehension, world interactions discovered and next verbs (silhouetted if locked) so that I plan experiments and hotbar loadouts.
Drag spell to hotbar; filter by school; insights journal page; "rumoured spells" section fed by NPC rumour hooks.

## Scope
- In: grimoire UI, school tabs, drag-to-hotbar, insight journal page, locked-verb silhouettes, rumoured spells list
- Out: hotbar (e06-spell-hotbar-ui)
- Out: final grimoire art (asset prompt beads)

## Notes
"World interactions discovered" lists property tags the player has personally affected with that spell — reinforcing the systemic model.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given 5 known spells across 3 schools, when the grimoire opens on the Fire tab, then only Fire spells are listed.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a spell with a locked next verb, when viewed, then the next verb shows as a silhouette with its unlock requirement text.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a spell dragged onto hotbar slot 4, when dropped, then slot 4 holds that spell.
- AC-4 [integration] Given no known spells (non-sorcerer start), when opened, then an empty state is shown without errors.
- AC-5 [integration] Given the player ignited 3 distinct property-tagged objects with Ember, when viewing Ember, then those 3 property tags are listed as discovered interactions.

items.title: Find books on bookshelves, enemies and as rewards
items.description:
## Why
The world rewards curiosity: bookshelves can contain books, and casters carry the books they learned from.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want to search bookshelves, loot books from enemy casters and receive books from quests or characters so that books come from everywhere, not just shops.
Bookshelf-tagged objects have searchable loot tables (mostly mundane lore, occasional spell book); creature casters optionally drop a book for one of their spells; quest/dialogue reward actions can grant books.

## Scope
- In: bookshelf search interaction, book entries in loot tables, caster book drop rule, grant-book action for quest/dialogue
- Out: specific placements (E24–E26 world content)
- Out: shops (mw-e21)

## Notes
Searching a bookshelf takes 2 s and makes a quiet noise (thief interplay).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a bookshelf-tagged object with a loot table containing a spell book, when searched with a fixed seed, then the book is added to inventory and the shelf becomes "searched" in world state.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a searched bookshelf, when searched again, then nothing new is granted.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a creature caster with dropsSpellBook=true, when killed, then its loot contains a book teaching one of its spells.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a dialogue/quest action grantBook, when executed, then the book is added to inventory.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a full inventory (if capacity limits exist), when a book is found, then it is placed on the ground at the player position rather than lost.

items.title: Persist known spells, study progress, languages and insights
items.description:
## Why
Losing a learned spell to a save bug would betray the core sorcerer reward loop.

## What
Serialize known spells + comprehension, per-book study progress, known languages, discovered insights, verb unlock counters into the versioned save with round-trip and migration tests.

## Scope
- In: learning save section, round-trip tests, migration scaffold
- Out: inventory contents (E17/E30)

## Notes
Unknown spell ids in a save (content removed) are dropped with a warning, not a crash.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given 4 known spells, 2 in-progress studies, 1 language and 2 insights, when saved and loaded, then all values are identical.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a save referencing a spell id no longer in content, when loaded, then the spell is dropped, a warning is logged and load succeeds.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a v1 learning save, when loaded by v2, then the migration test passes.

items.title: Document magic schools, spell data conventions and too-useful policy
items.description:
## Why
Twenty spells authored by different people must feel like one coherent magic system.

## What
docs/design/magic-schools.md: each school's fantasy, primary stimuli, colour tag for placeholder VFX, default loudness, miscast flavour; spell file template; naming for cue/icon/cover ids; testing template (effects + ≥2 property interactions); explicit "too useful is allowed" policy and the too-useful label.

## Scope
- In: design doc
- In: spell file template in src/content/spells/_template
- In: test file template
- Out: individual spells

## Notes
Schools in MVP: Fire, Frost, Storm, Arcane, Illusion, Alteration, Conjuration, Necromancy, Nature, Light, Shadow, Gravity, Time.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the spell template file, when validated by the spell schema, then it passes.
- AC-2 [content] Given the magic-schools doc, when checked by a docs test, then every school enum value in the schema has a section.
- AC-3 [manual] Given a designer new to the project, when authoring a fixture spell from the template, then they finish in ≤ 30 minutes without code changes.

items.title: Add Ember: precise ignition of flammable things
items.description:
## Why
Constitution example: ignite candles, ropes, oil and enemies — the gateway spell for systemic fire.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want a cheap, short-range ignition bolt so that I can light anything flammable precisely.
Slow projectile, low damage, strong heat stimulus at impact point (small radius). Carries a small light op.

## Scope
- In: Ember spell
- In: spell JSON + book item JSON, unit tests for effects, integration tests for world interactions, placeholder cue ids
- Out: final VFX/SFX/icon/book cover (asset prompt beads)
- Out: world placement of the book (E24–E26)

## Notes
School: Fire. Placeholder cues: vfx-spell-ember-cast, vfx-spell-ember-travel, vfx-spell-ember-impact, sfx-spell-ember-cast, sfx-spell-ember-impact. Icon: icon-spell-ember. Book cover: ui-book-cover-ember.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the spell data file, when validated and loaded, then it has a school, book item, vfxCue and sfxCue and casts in the headless sim.
- AC-2 [integration] Given any object tagged flammable, when hit by Ember, then it ignites within 1 sim second.
- AC-3 [integration] Given an object tagged wet, when hit by Ember, then it does not ignite and loses wet after 3 hits (steam) per E03 rules.

School: Light. Placeholder cues: vfx-spell-wisp-light-orb, sfx-spell-wisp-light-{spawn,hum-loop}. Icon: icon-spell-wisp-light. Book cover: ui-book-cover-wisp-light.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the spell data file, when validated and loaded, then it has a school, book item, vfxCue and sfxCue and casts in the headless sim.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a dark room with light level 0.05, when the wisp is present, then the light field within 5 m of it is ≥ 0.5.
- AC-3 [integration] Given any light-sensitive mechanism (tagged light-activated) within the wisp's radius above its threshold, when the wisp arrives, then it activates.
