- AC-5 [integration] Given the player carries a follow-wisp while sneaking, when a guard evaluates visibility, then the player's visibility score increases per the visibility model (stealth trade-off).
- AC-6 [unit] Given a Snuff/darkness effect overlapping the wisp, when resolved, then the wisp is extinguished early.

items.title: Add Prism Ray: a light beam that reflects off reflective surfaces
items.description:
## Why
Puzzle constitution: redirecting light. A reflecting beam turns mirrors and polished shields into puzzle pieces.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want a channeled beam of focused light that bounces off reflective surfaces so that I can power light mechanisms around corners and dazzle creatures.
Beam with light op and small heat; reflects up to 3 times off reflective-tagged objects; dazzles (blinded 2 s) creatures that look into it.

## Scope
- In: Prism Ray spell
- In: blinded status
- In: spell JSON + book item JSON, unit tests for effects, integration tests for world interactions, placeholder cue ids
- Out: final VFX/SFX/icon/book cover (asset prompt beads)
- Out: world placement of the book (E24–E26)

## Notes
School: Light. Placeholder cues: vfx-spell-prism-ray-beam, vfx-spell-prism-ray-reflect, sfx-spell-prism-ray-loop. Icon: icon-spell-prism-ray. Book cover: ui-book-cover-prism-ray.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the spell data file, when validated and loaded, then it has a school, book item, vfxCue and sfxCue and casts in the headless sim.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a reflective object angled at 45°, when the beam hits it, then the reflected beam continues at 90° and can activate a light-activated mechanism on the reflected path.
- AC-3 [integration] Given any object tagged reflective including a Frostglass ice sheet, when hit, then the beam reflects (property-based, not object-based).
- AC-4 [integration] Given a creature facing the caster within the beam, when hit, then it gains blinded for 2 s and its sight perception is disabled for that time.
- AC-5 [unit] Given more than 3 reflective surfaces in a row, when channeled, then the beam stops after the third reflection.

items.title: Add Snuff: extinguish all light sources in a radius
items.description:
## Why
Shadow magic that serves stealth: the sorcerer can create darkness like the thief extinguishing lights.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want to snuff every flame and magical light within 6 m so that I can plunge a room into darkness and use it to hide or disorient.
AoE that removes lit state from light-source objects and ends light ops; smothers small fires (not large blazes); quiet cast.

## Scope
- In: Snuff spell
- In: spell JSON + book item JSON, unit tests for effects, integration tests for world interactions, placeholder cue ids
- Out: final VFX/SFX/icon/book cover (asset prompt beads)
- Out: world placement of the book (E24–E26)

## Notes
School: Shadow. Placeholder cues: vfx-spell-snuff-pulse, sfx-spell-snuff-hush. Icon: icon-spell-snuff. Book cover: ui-book-cover-snuff.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the spell data file, when validated and loaded, then it has a school, book item, vfxCue and sfxCue and casts in the headless sim.
- AC-2 [integration] Given 5 lit candles and 1 torch within 6 m, when Snuff is cast, then all become unlit and the light field drops accordingly.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a burning object larger than the small-fire threshold, when Snuff is cast, then it remains burning.
- AC-4 [integration] Given guards in the darkened room, when they evaluate visibility of the player, then the reduced light level lowers the player's visibility score.
- AC-5 [unit] Given Snuff noise loudness, when cast, then emitted loudness is ≤ 20 (quiet).

items.title: Add Grasping Vines: roots burst up and restrain creatures
items.description:
## Why
Constitution example; restraint as a verb — and vines are organic, so fire and frost interact naturally.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want roots to erupt in a 3 m area and bind creatures for up to 6 s so that I can pin enemies, hold doors or stop a fleeing thief.
Spawns vine entities (tagged organic, flammable) that apply rooted to creatures inside; rooted breaks when its vine entity is destroyed or burns; only works on soil/stone ground, not water or wood floors above empty space.

## Scope
- In: Grasping Vines spell
- In: vine entity archetype
- In: spell JSON + book item JSON, unit tests for effects, integration tests for world interactions, placeholder cue ids
- Out: final VFX/SFX/icon/book cover (asset prompt beads)
- Out: world placement of the book (E24–E26)

## Notes
School: Nature. Placeholder cues: vfx-spell-grasping-vines-{erupt,hold,wither}, sfx-spell-grasping-vines-{erupt,creak}. Icon: icon-spell-grasping-vines. Book cover: ui-book-cover-grasping-vines.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the spell data file, when validated and loaded, then it has a school, book item, vfxCue and sfxCue and casts in the headless sim.
- AC-2 [integration] Given 3 creatures inside the area, when cast, then each is rooted for 6 s unless tagged too-large-to-root.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the vines are hit by any heat stimulus above ignition threshold, when they burn, then they are destroyed within 2 s and rooted ends early.
- AC-4 [integration] Given a strong creature with the break-free trait, when rooted, then it breaks free after 2 s.
- AC-5 [unit] Given cast onto a water surface, when resolved, then the cast fails with reason "invalid-surface" and mana is refunded.
- AC-6 [integration] Given a life stimulus source nearby (e.g. a second Vines cast), when overlapping, then vine duration refreshes (organic growth rule).

items.title: Add Animate Bones: raise nearby remains as a temporary servant
items.description:
## Why
Constitution example; summoning grounded in the world — no bones nearby, no servant.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want to assemble skeletal remains within 6 m into a temporary skeletal servant for 45 s so that the dungeon's dead fight for me.
Summon op requiring remains-tagged material; servant follows/attacks; crumbles back into remains (reusable) on expiry; the spell comes from a forbidden book.

## Scope
- In: Animate Bones spell
- In: skeletal servant archetype (reuses bestiary skeleton data if available)
- In: spell JSON + book item JSON, unit tests for effects, integration tests for world interactions, placeholder cue ids
- Out: final VFX/SFX/icon/book cover (asset prompt beads)
- Out: world placement of the book (E24–E26)

## Notes
School: Necromancy. Placeholder cues: vfx-spell-animate-bones-{assemble,crumble}, sfx-spell-animate-bones-{assemble,rattle,crumble}. Icon: icon-spell-animate-bones. Book cover: ui-book-cover-animate-bones.
Related: bestiary skeleton archetype from the creatures group; use a fixture archetype until it exists. Book is forbidden (e07-forbidden-books).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the spell data file, when validated and loaded, then it has a school, book item, vfxCue and sfxCue and casts in the headless sim.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a remains-tagged object within 6 m, when cast, then a servant with caster allegiance spawns at the remains location and the remains are consumed.
- AC-3 [integration] Given no remains in range, when cast, then the cast fizzles with a SpellFizzled event and full refund.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the servant expires, when 45 s pass, then a remains-tagged object is left at its position (reusable).
- AC-5 [integration] Given a hostile skeleton creature, when targeted with Animate Bones, then it is not converted (only inert remains qualify).
- AC-6 [integration] Given a lawful NPC witness, when the player casts Animate Bones in view, then a ContrabandWitnessed event fires (forbidden school).

items.title: Add Polymorph: temporarily turn a creature into a harmless animal
items.description:
## Why
Constitution example; transformation that solves fights, social problems and puzzles in unexpected ways.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want to turn a creature into a small animal (e.g. a chicken-like critter) for 20 s so that I can neutralise threats, sneak past guards or make a heavy creature light enough to Mage Hand.
Transform op to a small-creature archetype; large/boss creatures tagged immune-transform resist; the critter form has its own properties (small, light, flammable) that other spells interact with.

## Scope
- In: Polymorph spell
- In: critter archetype for the transformed form
- In: spell JSON + book item JSON, unit tests for effects, integration tests for world interactions, placeholder cue ids
- Out: final VFX/SFX/icon/book cover (asset prompt beads)
- Out: world placement of the book (E24–E26)

## Notes
School: Alteration. Placeholder cues: vfx-spell-polymorph-{poof-in,poof-out}, sfx-spell-polymorph-{poof,critter-cluck}. Icon: icon-spell-polymorph. Book cover: ui-book-cover-polymorph.
TOO USEFUL — INTENTIONALLY ALLOWED (constitution §4). Do not nerf this spell to prevent sequence breaks or cheese; encounters and puzzles must tolerate it. Balance only via mana/cast time/cooldown, never by adding pairwise exceptions.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the spell data file, when validated and loaded, then it has a school, book item, vfxCue and sfxCue and casts in the headless sim.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a humanoid guard, when polymorphed, then it becomes the critter archetype for 20 s with its alert memory intact and restores exactly afterwards.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a polymorphed creature now tagged small and light, when grabbed by Mage Hand/Telekinetic Throw, then it can be lifted (properties of the new form apply).
- AC-4 [integration] Given a creature tagged immune-transform, when targeted, then it resists and emits SpellResisted.
- AC-5 [integration] Given the critter is killed and Polymorph uses onFormDeath=revert, when killed, then the original reverts with 1 HP and a stagger status.
- AC-6 [unit] Given Polymorph cast on the caster via a reflective surface bounce (if a beam reflection returns), when resolved, then the caster is transformed — intentionally allowed.

items.title: Add Stasis: freeze one object or creature in time
items.description:
## Why
Time magic creates novel puzzle and combat verbs: hold a falling gate, stop a swinging blade, pause an enemy.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want to lock a single target in time for 5 s so that I can freeze moving traps, suspend falling objects or stop an attacker mid-swing.
Stasis status: zero velocity, immune to damage and forces, mechanisms paused; stored impulses from hits apply on release (capped).

## Scope
- In: Stasis spell
- In: stasis status with stored impulse
- In: spell JSON + book item JSON, unit tests for effects, integration tests for world interactions, placeholder cue ids
- Out: final VFX/SFX/icon/book cover (asset prompt beads)
- Out: world placement of the book (E24–E26)

## Notes
School: Time. Placeholder cues: vfx-spell-stasis-{lock,release}, sfx-spell-stasis-{lock,release}. Icon: icon-spell-stasis. Book cover: ui-book-cover-stasis.
TOO USEFUL — INTENTIONALLY ALLOWED (constitution §4). Do not nerf this spell to prevent sequence breaks or cheese; encounters and puzzles must tolerate it. Balance only via mana/cast time/cooldown, never by adding pairwise exceptions.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the spell data file, when validated and loaded, then it has a school, book item, vfxCue and sfxCue and casts in the headless sim.
- AC-2 [integration] Given a moving mechanism (swinging blade, falling portcullis), when stasis is applied, then it halts for 5 s and resumes its prior motion afterwards.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a creature in stasis struck by forces totalling 300 N·s, when stasis ends, then the stored impulse (capped at 200 N·s) applies at once.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a creature in stasis, when damage is applied, then health is unchanged during stasis.
- AC-5 [unit] Given a creature tagged boss or immune-time, when targeted, then duration is reduced to 1 s.

items.title: Build the spell combination test suite and greybox spell gallery
items.description:
## Why
Emergent combinations are the point of magic; a suite proves they emerge from properties and catches regressions when E03 rules change.

## What
A generated integration test matrix: for every pair of stimulus types emitted by catalogue spells (heat, cold, force, light, moisture, charge, life, decay) applied in both orders to a fixture set of property-tagged generic objects and creatures, assert deterministic, rule-consistent outcomes (golden snapshots). Plus curated scenario tests (Wellspring → Arc Lash chain, Wellspring → Frostglass bridge, Gravity Well → Thunderclap scatter, Gust → Fire spread, Polymorph → Telekinetic Throw) expressed via properties. Plus a greybox "spell gallery" room exhibiting every property for e2e/manual play.

## Scope
- In: combination matrix generator, golden snapshots, curated scenario tests, greybox gallery scene, e2e smoke of the gallery
- Out: E03 rule changes (Core group) — the suite reports, it does not fix

## Notes
Golden updates require an explicit reviewed flag in the PR. Suite runs headless in < 60 s.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given every ordered pair of catalogue stimulus types and the fixture object set, when run, then outcomes match golden snapshots and two runs produce identical hashes.
- AC-2 [integration] Given Wellspring then Arc Lash on 3 creatures in the puddle, when resolved, then all receive charge damage (conduction through wet).
- AC-3 [integration] Given Wellspring then Frostglass on a pit filled with water, when resolved, then a walkable ice surface exists across the pit.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a new spell added to the catalogue emitting an unseen stimulus type, when the suite runs, then it fails listing the missing pair coverage.
- AC-5 [perf] Given the full suite, when run in CI, then it completes in ≤ 60 s.
- AC-6 [e2e] Given the greybox spell gallery, when a scripted run casts every P1 spell at its gallery station, then no console errors occur and each station reports its expected property change.
- AC-7 [manual] Given a 30-minute playtest in the gallery, when testers experiment freely, then they report at least 3 combinations nobody told them about.

items.title: Generate bookshop stock from regional pools and school specialties
items.description:
## Why
Bookshops should be genuinely exciting destinations with different inventories per settlement (constitution §4).

## What
As a designer, I want to author a bookshop as data (region, specialties, pools, rules) on top of the generic shop system so that each settlement's bookshop feels distinct without code.
BookshopDefinition: shopId (E20), region, specialtySchools[] with weight multipliers, staplePool (always stocked), regionalPool, rarePool, secretPool, rotation rules, bookseller profile id. Stock generation is deterministic from world seed + shop id + rotation period.

## Scope
- In: bookshop schema, stock generator for staples/regional/specialty, integration with e20 shop buy/sell
- Out: rotation (e21-rotating-stock)
- Out: rare/secret (own beads)
- Out: Briar Glen shop content (world-content group, E24)

## Notes
The same book may appear in multiple regional pools; uniques are tracked globally so a unique book only ever exists once.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a bookshop with 3 staple books and a regional pool of 10, when stock is generated, then all 3 staples plus N regional books (per rule) are present.
- AC-2 [unit] Given specialty Fire with weight 3×, when stock is generated over 1000 seeds, then Fire books are selected ≈3× as often as unweighted books (±10%).
- AC-3 [unit] Given the same world seed, shop id and period, when generated twice, then stock is identical.
- AC-4 [integration] Given the player buys a book, when the transaction completes via the e20 shop system, then the book is in inventory and removed from stock.
- AC-5 [content] Given a bookshop referencing a non-book item in a book pool, when validated, then validation fails.

items.title: Rotate bookshop stock on an in-game schedule
items.description:
## Why
Rotating inventory gives a reason to return to the bookshop after each expedition.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want the bookshop's non-staple shelves to change every few in-game days so that revisiting is worthwhile.
Rotation period in in-game days; rotating slots re-roll from pools excluding books the player already owns or knows (configurable); sold-out items restock only at rotation; state persists.

## Scope
- In: rotation scheduler, exclusion rules, persistence of current stock and last rotation
- Out: rare/unique books (e21-rare-stock)

## Notes
Rotation triggers on in-game time crossing the boundary, including while the player is away (lazy evaluation on shop open).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a rotation period of 3 days, when in-game time advances 3 days and the shop opens, then rotating slots re-roll exactly once.
- AC-2 [unit] Given in-game time advances 9 days while away, when the shop opens, then stock equals what 3 sequential rotations would produce (deterministic).
- AC-3 [unit] Given excludeKnown=true, when rotating, then no book teaching an already-known spell appears in rotating slots.
- AC-4 [unit] Given a pool smaller than the slot count after exclusions, when rotating, then remaining slots are filled with lore books or left empty — never duplicates.
- AC-5 [integration] Given a save mid-period, when reloaded, then stock and next rotation time are unchanged.

items.title: Stock rare and unique books gated by world state conditions
items.description:
## Why
Rare books are the thrill of a bookshop: the one copy of a legendary grimoire appearing after you help the bookseller.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want rare books that appear only under conditions (quest completed, disposition level, day of week, region event) and unique books that exist once in the world so that bookshop visits can surprise me.
Conditions evaluated against the world state store and dialogue disposition; unique books tracked globally; a rare book may be "reserved" for the player for N days.

## Scope
- In: condition evaluation, unique registry, reservation window
- Out: secret back-room stock (e21-secret-stock)

## Notes
Conditions reuse the shared condition language from E22/E23 if available; otherwise a minimal condition set with a migration note.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a rare book conditioned on world fact "helped_bookseller", when the fact is false, then the book is not stocked; when true, it appears at next shop open.
- AC-2 [unit] Given a unique book already looted from a dungeon, when a shop would stock it, then it is skipped.
- AC-3 [unit] Given a reserved rare book with a 5-day window, when 5 days pass without purchase, then it leaves stock and returns to the rare pool.
- AC-4 [content] Given a rare entry with an unknown condition key, when validated, then validation fails.

items.title: Reveal secret back-room stock through dialogue, trust or discovery
items.description:
## Why
Secret inventory rewards curiosity and relationships — the "do you have anything… special?" moment.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want some bookshops to have hidden stock unlocked by a password, high disposition, a quest, or physically finding the back room so that secrets exist even in shops.
Secret pool gated by unlock method; can be accessed by a thief breaking in (stolen goods flagged on removal).

## Scope
- In: secret pool unlock via dialogue action/disposition/world fact, physical back-room container hook
- Out: dialogue content and passwords (world-content group)

## Notes
Taking from the back room without buying marks books stolen (e21-stolen-forbidden-stock).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a dialogue action unlockSecretStock, when executed, then the secret pool becomes purchasable for this shop.
- AC-2 [unit] Given disposition below the threshold and no other unlock, when the shop opens, then secret items are not listed.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player takes a secret-stock book from the back-room container without buying, when removed, then the book is flagged stolen with owner = the shop.
- AC-4 [unit] Given secret stock unlocked, when saved and reloaded, then it remains unlocked.

items.title: Price books by rarity, condition, legality, region and disposition
items.description:
## Why
Gold should have meaningful uses (E20); expensive books are aspirational goals.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want book prices that reflect rarity, condition, forbidden premium, regional demand and my relationship with the bookseller so that saving up for a grimoire matters.
price = base(rarity, tier) × condition × legality premium × region demand(school) × disposition modifier; sell-back price for books the player sells (booksellers pay more for books in their specialty).

## Scope
- In: pricing function (pure, data-configured), sell-back pricing, integer rounding rules
- Out: generic currency/transactions (e20-shop-system)

## Notes
All arithmetic in integer copper to avoid float drift; 100% coverage as an economy rule.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given base 200, damaged ×0.5, forbidden ×1.8, region ×1.0 and neutral disposition, when priced, then the price is 180.
- AC-2 [unit] Given friendly disposition −10% modifier, when priced, then the price is reduced by 10% (rounded to nearest copper).
- AC-3 [unit] Given the player sells a book in the shop's specialty school, when priced, then sell-back is the specialty rate (e.g. 40% of buy) instead of the default (25%).
- AC-4 [unit] Given any combination of modifiers, when priced, then the result is an integer ≥ 1 (property test).
- AC-5 [content] Given a pricing config with a negative multiplier, when validated, then validation fails.

items.title: Handle stolen and forbidden books in bookshop trade
items.description:
## Why
Some books are stolen or forbidden (constitution §4) — trading them should carry risk and create thief/sorcerer crossover.

## What
As a sorcerer or thief, I want booksellers to react to stolen and forbidden books — refusing, fencing at a discount, or selling forbidden stock under the counter — so that illicit books have a market with consequences.
Bookseller profile flags: buysStolen, sellsForbidden, reportsContraband. Selling a book stolen from this very shop triggers recognition. Forbidden stock is only shown when no lawful witnesses are nearby.

## Scope
- In: stolen-owner tracking in trade, bookseller legality flags, witness check for forbidden sales, recognition consequence
- Out: guard response behaviour (E11)
- Out: forbidden reading consequences (e07-forbidden-books)

## Notes
Stolen flag comes from the E17/E10 ownership model — Related: thief group stealing/ownership bead.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [unit] Given a bookseller with buysStolen=false, when offered a stolen book, then the sale is refused with reason "stolen".
- AC-2 [unit] Given buysStolen=true, when buying a stolen book, then price is the fence rate (default 50% of normal sell-back).
- AC-3 [integration] Given the player tries to sell a book stolen from this same shop, when offered, then the bookseller recognises it: disposition drops and a world fact "caught_selling_back" is recorded.
- AC-4 [integration] Given sellsForbidden=true and a lawful NPC within perception range, when the shop opens, then forbidden stock is hidden until the witness leaves.
- AC-5 [integration] Given reportsContraband=true, when the player sells a forbidden book, then a ContrabandReported event fires.

items.title: Give booksellers identity profiles, wants and rumour hooks
items.description:
## Why
Merchants have identities (E20); a bookseller who wants a specific tome or gossips about a rare book elsewhere drives exploration.

## What
As a designer, I want a bookseller profile (personality tags, favoured/disliked schools, wanted books list, rumours about books elsewhere, greeting variants keyed on player class and known spells) so that the dialogue group can make each bookseller memorable.
Exposes conditions/variables to the dialogue runtime: bookseller.wants(bookId), bookseller.rumour(), player.knowsSchool(school). Wanted books pay a bonus or unlock rare stock.

## Scope
- In: profile schema, dialogue variables/conditions, wanted-book bonus, rumour selection rule (points to books in other shops or dungeons)
- Out: actual dialogue writing and NPC characters (world-content/narrative groups)

## Notes
Rumours reference book ids + a location hint string authored in content; they add entries to the grimoire "rumoured spells" section (e07-grimoire-ui).
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a profile with wantedBooks [X], when the player sells book X, then the bonus price applies and world fact "delivered_X" is set.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the dialogue runtime queries bookseller.rumour(), when the player already owns the rumoured book, then a different rumour is chosen or none.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a rumour is heard, when resolved, then the rumoured spell appears in the grimoire rumoured list with its location hint.
- AC-4 [content] Given a profile referencing an unknown book id in wantedBooks, when validated, then validation fails.

items.title: Browse bookshop shelves with covers, previews and known markers
items.description:
## Why
The bookshop should feel like browsing a magical shop, not a spreadsheet.

## What
As a sorcerer, I want to browse books by shelf/school with cover art, price, a first-page preview, comprehension estimate and "already known"/"stolen"/"forbidden" markers so that choosing a book is exciting and informed.
Extends the generic shop UI with book-specific panels; sell tab shows sell-back prices and wanted-book highlights.

## Scope
- In: bookshop UI panels, preview (reuses reader component), markers, sell tab highlights, keyboard/gamepad navigation
- Out: generic shop UI (E20)
- Out: final cover art (asset prompt beads per book)

## Notes
Placeholder covers: school-coloured leather with title text until art arrives.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [integration] Given a stocked shop, when the UI opens, then books are grouped by school shelf with price and cover (placeholder if no art).
- AC-2 [integration] Given a book teaching a known spell, when listed, then it shows an "Already known" marker.
- AC-3 [integration] Given the preview action, when used, then the first page renders via the reader component (garbled if language unknown).
- AC-4 [integration] Given insufficient gold, when attempting to buy, then the buy button is disabled with a reason and no transaction occurs.
- AC-5 [e2e] Given the greybox testbed fixture shop, when a scripted player buys a book, then it appears in inventory and gold decreases by the listed price.

items.title: Provide a bookshop authoring template, validator and fixture shop
items.description:
## Why
The world-content group must author the Briar Glen bookshop (and future ones) purely as data.

## What
Template src/content/bookshops/_template.json with every field documented, a CLI/dev validator (pnpm validate:bookshops) reporting stock simulation over 10 rotations, and a non-Briar-Glen fixture shop ("Testbed Tomes") in the greybox testbed exercising every rule.

## Scope
- In: template, validator CLI with stock simulation report, fixture shop, authoring notes in docs/design/bookshops.md
- Out: Briar Glen bookshop content (world-content group, E24)

## Notes
Report flags pools that can never appear (all conditions unsatisfiable) and uniques duplicated across shops.
items.acceptance:
- AC-1 [content] Given the template, when validated, then it passes the bookshop schema.
- AC-2 [integration] Given the fixture shop, when the validator simulates 10 rotations, then it prints stock per period and exits 0.
- AC-3 [integration] Given a shop whose rare book condition references a fact no content ever sets, when validated, then the validator warns "unreachable stock".
- AC-4 [content] Given two shops listing the same unique book, when validated, then validation fails.
